importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types — steel truss vs PEB vs tensile membrane vs arch roof are visually distinct structures. Buyers scan images first to confirm the structural form and finish quality matches their venue vision before reading any specs.

Span width, structure type, and roofing material are primary shortlisting criteria — a seller who cannot cover the required span or supply the required structural system cannot be engaged regardless of price.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in this category; market is fragmented across regional fabricators and contractors — buyers search by capability, portfolio, and geography, not brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Turnkey project buyers evaluate contractor track record, completed project portfolio, and regional service capability before committing; seller identity is a qualification signal after spec fit is confirmed.

Per-sq-ft price varies substantially with span width, structure type, and roofing material — buyers use listed price as a budget entry point after spec shortlisting, with final price always negotiated as a project quote.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Very large institutional or government contracts may be quoted as lump-sum project value, but per sq ft remains the universal comparison benchmark across all sub-segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per project (lump sum) creates real price comparison confusion — unit must be shown alongside price so buyers can normalise and compare across listings accurately.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Span width is the primary structural determinant — a seller cannot supply a 40 m clear-span structure if they only fabricate up to 20 m, and material, section size, and cost scale non-linearly with span, making it the single largest price driver.

Roofing material (Galvalume sheet vs PPGI vs Sandwich Panel vs Tensile Fabric vs Polycarbonate) drives significant price delta and determines thermal, acoustic, and aesthetic performance — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Bay length (column spacing along the length of the structure) directly determines the number of columns, purlin spans, and total steel tonnage — a key cost driver that buyers and structural engineers specify alongside span width.

Clear height at eave or ridge determines usable interior volume for seating, stage, and HVAC — auditorium buyers specify minimum clear height as a functional requirement that gates supplier eligibility.

IS 875 wind zone and IS 1893 seismic zone compliance are mandatory structural design inputs for public assembly buildings — buyers in high-wind or seismic zones must confirm the supplier designs to the correct zone.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Clear span width is the single most critical structural requirement — it determines whether a seller's fabrication capability and design system can physically deliver the structure, and it is the primary cost driver.

Structure type (Truss System vs PEB vs Dome vs Space Frame) defines the fabrication methodology and supplier specialisation — sellers who only do steel truss cannot supply a tensile or geodesic dome, making this a hard routing filter.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Roofing material determines thermal comfort, acoustic performance, and cost — sellers need this to confirm they supply the required cladding system and to price the project accurately.
